rows: Storm spotter measured a 60 MPH wind gust in Harker Heights.
Storm spotter measured a 70 MPH wind gust. The emergency manager reported a few mobile homes were damaged.
A roof of a barn and a garden shed were blown away.

At least 20 mobile homes were damaged or destroyed. Several were rolled off their foundations and virtually disintegrated. Numerous barns and outbuildings were destroyed. Four people were injured. Winds were estimated at 80 MPH.

At least two mobile homes in Moffat were pushed more than three feet off of their foundations. A garage was destroyed and debris covered a nearby road. Several other structures including outbuildings were damaged or destroyed. The Moffat Fire Chief estimated winds in excess of 70…
Baseball-size hail was reportedly still melting at daybreak the next morning.
A few trees and large limbs were blown down.

Several large trees uprooted and large tree limbs snapped. One huge tree fell on a transmission repair shop. Numerous power lines were blown down, as well as a light at a ballfield. A sign at a bank was ripped off. Power was out to about 1,200 people.
Street lights were damaged on the south edge of Temple.
Penny-size hail reported from Salado to near Belton.
Nickel-size hail was reported in Temple at 4:17 PM CST and in Troy at 4:30 PM CST.
Off-duty meteorologists reported a tornado. This tornado was also filmed by a TV station near Troy. A few home roofs were damaged.
Tornado observed on military base...no damage reported. ASOS measured 71 MPH with tornado on runway.
Penny to nickel-size hail fell from Morgan's Point Resort to White Hall.
High winds caused a power line to fall across Highway 190 onto a car, and to tear a hole in a church roof on Highway 195. About 3,500 residents and businesses were without power in Killeen.

A tornado was seen touching down near Highway 2410 south of Rancier Road. Fort Hood military personnel then saw it 5 minutes later near the base. The tornado damaged a bicycle shop and a few other buildings including houses. Damage was mainly to walls and roofs.

In Belton, amateur radio operators reported power flashes and a few downed trees. In and around Temple, power flashes were reported and numerous roofs, fences, and signs were damaged. One fence which was knocked down was anchored with cement pillars. Guests at a motel which lost …
The roofs were torn off of several structures at the intersection of Calhoun and 13th Streets.
Golfball-size hail was reported at the intersection of Highways 36 and 317.
Golfball-size hail was reported at the airport.

Brief tornadoes were reported near Fire Station #2 in Belton and near the intersection of I-35 and Highway 190. No damage was reported.
Golfball-size hail broke skylights and car windshields.
Golfball to baseball-size hail was reported.
A television meteorologist observed a brief tornado west of Holland. No damage was reported.
Golfball-size hail was reported between Belton and Little River Academy.
Power lines and poles were blown down in Killeen.

Numerous trees had large limbs broken. A few trees were uprooted or snapped at the trunk. Several storage buildings were damaged, and a few homes suffered minor roof damage. Additional homes were damaged by falling trees and limbs.
Trees were blown down and a hotel under construction was damaged at I-35 and exit 286.
A house was damaged and trees were uprooted near the intersection of Armstrong Drive and Elmer King Road.

A downburst damage swath which began near Salado continued east with additional tree and roof damage in Little River Academy. The most substantial damage was observed between Heidenheimer and Rogers where several mobile homes had roof damage or were moved. Two large barns had tin…
Damage to roofs and structures reported.

Two foot diameter trees were snapped in half along Highway 95 in Little River Academy. Numerous signs and billboards were blown down between Salado and Little River Academy. Trees fell on and damaged cars in Little River.
Trees were blown down and the high school lost some bricks. A historic home and a restaurant in Salado suffered roof damage.
Nickel-size hail was reported near the Youngsport community.
Penny-size hail was reported along Highway 95.
Rock facing was removed from the wall of a commercial building.
Power lines were blown down on Main Street and Smith Dairy Road in Belton. Numerous trees and large limbs were also blown down across the city...including several on FM 439 near Lake Belton.
Trees were knocked down in the western portion of the county.
Winds of 60 MPH were estimated in the south end of town.
Two 18 wheelers were overturned. A 35-foot communications tower on top of a building was folded over. 70 MPH winds were estimated in the area.
Penny hail fell 3 miles west of Belton.
A trailer home was blown against a fence at an RV dealership and another trailer home was lifted up and tossed on top of a third trailer. The metal roof of a nearby business was peeled back.

Strong thunderstorm winds damaged a manufactured home near Rogers. Part of the siding of the home was ripped off and part of the metal roof was peeled back.

A few boat docks were damaged at Frank's Marina on Lake Belton. Shore moorings were uprooted and underwater anchorages were sheared off.
